SnapBoard — install in 3 steps
==============================

Windows-style window snapping + clipboard history for macOS 15 or later.


1. DRAG SnapBoard onto the Applications folder in this window.


2. OPEN TERMINAL AND RUN THIS ONE LINE:

       xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/SnapBoard.app

   This is NOT optional. SnapBoard is signed with an ad-hoc signature
   (an internal test build, not a paid Apple Developer certificate).
   Without this line macOS says "SnapBoard is damaged and can't be
   opened" — that is Gatekeeper wording it badly. The app is fine.


3. LAUNCH IT, THEN GRANT ACCESSIBILITY.

       open /Applications/SnapBoard.app

   A setup window appears with a button through to the right settings
   pane. Turn ON the switch next to SnapBoard.

   The setup window closes by itself once it works.

   Nothing snaps or pastes until this is granted — the app cannot move
   another app's window without it.


HOW TO USE IT
-------------
   Control+Command+Left     snap window to left half
   Control+Command+Right    snap to right half
   Control+Command+Up       maximize
   Control+Command+Down     restore, or minimize

   Press Left/Right again on an already-snapped window to send it to
   your next monitor.

   Command+Shift+V          clipboard history
     type to search, arrows to move, Return to paste,
     Shift+Return pastes as plain text, Command+P pins, Esc closes

   Screenshots land in history if you use CONTROL+Command+Shift+4
   (with Control, they go to the clipboard). Plain Command+Shift+4
   saves a file to the Desktop instead and will not be captured.


THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE YOU RUN THIS ON A WORK MACHINE
----------------------------------------------------
 * Clipboard history is stored UNENCRYPTED as plain JSON at
     ~/Library/Application Support/SnapBoard/history.json
   Everything you copy goes in there, including anything you paste out
   of a password vault that does not mark itself as concealed. Check
   your company policy. You can set retention to 7 days, or quit the
   app when handling sensitive material.

 * If your Mac is managed by your company, IT may block Accessibility
   for apps that are not on their approved list. If the switch will not
   stay on, that is why, and only IT can change it.

 * If a new build is sent to you, macOS may ask for Accessibility
   again. Remove the old SnapBoard entry in the list (select, press
   minus) and re-add the new one.


TO UNINSTALL
------------
   Quit from the menu bar icon, then:
       rm -rf /Applications/SnapBoard.app
       rm -rf ~/Library/Application\ Support/SnapBoard

   The second line deletes your clipboard history.


Report anything broken to Thiru.
